category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.title and rationale focus only on E1.2 within Lesson 2; no cross-reference to Lesson 1's sides/symmetry work or to Lesson 3's congruence (which builds on matching/decomposing). The pair sits in isolation rather than bridging the unit's arc.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add an explicit bridge in expanded_walkthrough or teacher_script: e.g., 'Yesterday Symmy SORTED shapes by sides — today we DECOMPOSE them into smaller shapes. Tomorrow we test if two shapes are CONGRUENT — same idea, MATCHING the parts.' Tie to Day 1 sides/angles vocabulary that the children already learned.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.recovery_moves = ['Use a transparent grid overlay.', 'Drill count, dont judge by spread.', 'Multiple rearrangements.'] — concrete but not branched by what the diagnostic told you, and no research is cited (this is a classic Piagetian conservation-of-area trap; Battista on spatial reasoning, or Outhred & Mitchelmore 2000 on area measurement, would anchor it).
category_feedback.required_fix: Branch the recovery: if the child counts correctly but still claims spread = more, do the transparent-grid overlay; if the child miscounts (skips/double-counts tiles), drop back to one-to-one tile tagging with a finger before re-tackling conservation. Cite Piaget's conservation-of-area task or Battista's spatial-reasoning research in the rationale field.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: consolidation.exit_routine = "Each child rearranges 4 tiles 2 ways: 'My 4 tiles can look like ___ AND ___. Area stays ___.'" — a sentence frame, but Flippy and Symmy have no memorable quotable refrain that children carry between lessons. Compare to the rubric's Level 4 example ('HOO knows the sounds? YOU do!').
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Flippy a distinctive refrain children chant back at every consolidation, e.g., 'Same tiles, SAME area — Flippy's rule!' or 'Rearrange, rearrange — area DOESN'T change!' Quote it in teacher_script and have children echo it in the exit_routine so it carries to Lessons 3-5.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.rationale: 'child sees an L-shape made of 6 tiles and a 2x3 rectangle made of 6 tiles, says the L-shape looks bigger so has more area' — accurate but not named in research-grounded terms. Children also do not get to invent/refine/compare strategies; the action steps prescribe the moves rather than soliciting strategies for comparison.
category_feedback.required_fix: Name the misconception as Piagetian conservation-of-area failure (or Battista on area-as-count vs perimeter conflation) in expanded_walkthrough.rationale. In action step 4, add a strategy-share: 'Two pairs share their arrangements. Class compares: did anyone find a way without re-counting? Did anyone PREDICT before counting?' Let children compare counting-each-time vs. predicting-then-verifying.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Worksheet Part 2 ('Decompose a hexagon into 6 triangles') introduces a hexagon-into-triangles decomposition that the lesson did not explicitly model — the lesson uses square unit tiles into rectangles/L-shapes/rows. This is a reasonable transfer task but the deliberate variation is not justified anywhere in worksheet.teacher_notes or worksheet_brief.
category_feedback.required_fix: Either (a) add a brief hexagon-into-triangles demo in lesson minds_on or action so the worksheet practises what the lesson taught, OR (b) keep the transfer but justify it in worksheet.teacher_notes: 'Part 2 deliberately VARIES the decomposition (hexagon into triangles, not square tiles into rectangles) to verify children generalize area-conservation beyond unit squares.'
